surprises.description: Revenue was expected around $297 million, with the preview’s informal “whisper” at above $300 million; Manhattan reported a record $306 million, beating consensus and clearing that higher bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total quarterly revenue rose 11% to a record $306 million, exceeding the $300 million mark for the first time and beating expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q3'26 Consensus | $297.0M”; the preview also says “The functional whisper is ‘revenue above $300M.’”

surprises.description: Cloud revenue was expected at about $130 million and roughly 24% growth, with services expected to be about $133 million. Instead, cloud reached $134 million and grew 28%, overtaking services for the first time.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 cloud revenue grew 28% year-over-year to $134 million, accelerating from 24% in Q1 and 26% in Q2, with cloud revenue surpassing services revenue for the first time.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cloud subscription rev. | ~$130M (guide-anchored)” and “Services revenue | ~$133M”; the preview also calls ~$132M+ and approximately 25% growth a clear positive.

surprises.description: The quarter-end RPO dollar amount landed within the preview’s expected range, but its 25% year-over-year growth was ahead of the preview’s roughly 20–22% estimate. Management also raised its full-year RPO growth outlook to 21%, above the prior 18–20% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO increased 25% year-over-year to $2.59 billion (up 5% sequentially), and the company raised its full-year RPO growth outlook to 21%, up from the prior 18%-20% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview derived quarter-end RPO of “~$2.58–2.62B” and described it as “~+20–22%”; it also said the FY exit target was “$2.62–2.68B, ‘toward high end.’”

surprises.description: The full-year outlook exceeded the preview’s already-raised bull-case thresholds: revenue guidance is now $1.176–$1.178 billion versus the preview’s $1.170 billion-plus bar, and adjusted EPS is $5.54–$5.56 versus a base expectation of about $5.50. The $291 million Q4 revenue guide is also above the roughly $287 million implied by the prior full-year midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q4 total revenue down to about $291 million reflecting retail peak seasonality, with full-year revenue of $1.176-$1.178 billion and full-year adjusted EPS raised to $5.54-$5.56.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says investors wanted FY revenue “~$1,170M+” and adjusted EPS “toward $5.55+”; its prior-guidance arithmetic implied Q4 revenue of “only ~$287M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was expected at $1.46; the reported $1.55 was a clear beat. It also exceeded the preview’s bull-case range ceiling of $1.58 only in neither direction? Actually it falls within that range, while still well above the base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 14% to $1.55 … both beating expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Q3'26 Consensus | $1.46”; the preview’s base scenario was “$1.46–1.50.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin was expected around 36.9%; it came in at 37.6%, a 70-basis-point beat of the guide-anchored expectation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gives “Adj. operating margin … ~36–37%” and identifies “~36.9%” as the guide.

surprises.description: The preview noted that GAAP EPS had declined year over year in both Q1 and Q2. In Q3 it grew 8% to $1.04 and beat expectations, reversing that recent pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS grew 8% to $1.04 … both beating expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview notes that “GAAP EPS was down y/y in both Q1 and Q2.”

surprises.description: The fourth consecutive record bookings quarter was anticipated, but the preview did not flag that year-to-date deal volume would already exceed all of 2025. That cumulative volume is an additional sign of stronger bookings momentum than the preview quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company delivered its fourth consecutive record bookings quarter, with year-to-date deal volume already surpassing full-year 2025 total deal volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says Q2 followed “three consecutive record bookings quarters” and lists a “Fourth straight record bookings quarter” in its scenarios.

surprises.description: The preview expected pipeline color and said early Editions wins could be incremental upside, but did not anticipate partner-sourced deals increasing more than fourfold year over year. First Enterprise and Essentials wins were also reported; material revenue impact is still expected only in the second half of 2027, rather than being a near-term revenue driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New Editions packaging launched in Q3 with first Enterprise and Essentials Edition wins, partner-sourced deals up more than 4x year-over-year, with material Editions revenue impact expected in the second half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says Editions launched only about a week before quarter-end, so “Expect pipeline color, not revenue,” and calls early wins incremental upside.

surprises.description: Management explicitly endorsed 2027 consensus, including 20% cloud growth and continued operating-margin expansion. This provided forward validation against the preview’s concern that 2027 could bring elevated AI and go-to-market spending pressure on margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management endorsed 2027 consensus estimates as appropriate, including 20% cloud revenue growth, low single-digit services growth, and continued operating margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flags “Early signaling of elevated AI/go-to-market spend for 2027” as a risk and asks for 2027 framing.
